To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the lattice parameters of an epitaxially-grown silicon layer on a sapphire substrate by convergent-bean electron diffraction, and that the lattice compression in Si is anisotropic and depends on the distance from Si-Sapphire interface.

the local lattice parameters of a Si (100) layer grown on an Al2O3 (1102) were determined by CBED without any assumption of the crystal symmetry, and that an anisotropic lattice parameter was detected in the Si (100) plane.

an anisotropic lattice parameter was detected by convergent-beamediffraction for the first time in a Si-layer grown on a sappire substrate, and it was shown to be related to anisotropy in carrier mobility in the Si-layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of lattice parameters of a silicon (110) layer grown on an insulating sapphire (110) substrate.
the local lattice parameter determination of an Si (001) film grown on a saphire substrate.
the anisotropic lattice deformation in a Si layer grown on a substrate, which is caused by lattice mismatch between Si and substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a lattice parameter anisotropy was clearly detected for a Si layer on a sapphire substrate.
the anisotropic lattice parameter of the Si layer was caused by the strain induced by the lattice mismatch between the Si layer and sapphire substrate.
the anisotropic lattice parameters determined by CBED are the origin of the anisotropic carrier mobility of the Si-layer.

the lattice parameters determined by CBED were successfully used as a probe to understand anisotropy in the carrier transport in the Si-layer grown on a sappire (1102) substrat.
an anisotropic lattice deformation in a Si layer grown on a substrate with a different crystal structure was detected and explained by the lattice mismatch between the Si and the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
an anisotropic lattice parameter can be determined by CBED without assuming any lattice symmetry.

convergent-beam techniques can provide accurate lattice parameters of thin films, and that the anisotropic lattice parameters are very important for the understanding of the anisotropic properties of thin films.

the lattice compression and anisotropy in the Si layer can be determined by convergent beam electron diffraction (CBED) and that the anisotropies of the carrier mobility in the Si-layer can be explained in terms of those lattice parameters.
